data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The distinction is that idempotency is an intrinsic algebraic property of the operation (context-independent: f\u2218f = f), while safety is an extrinsic relational property (context-dependent: the operation preserves the invariants of a specific system). An append-only log requires idempotency from its writers, not merely safety, because without it, at-least-once delivery can produce unbounded log growth and eventual system failure \u2014 safety of invariants does not prevent resource exhaustion from duplicate entries.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If duplicate entries can be garbage-collected or compacted without breaking deterministic replay, then unbounded growth is not a real concern and safety suffices.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the system has a bounded retry count or time-to-live for retries, resource exhaustion may not occur in practice.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If consumer-side deduplication is computationally cheap and the log can grow arbitrarily large, then idempotency at the writer is unnecessary overhead.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Consider an append-only log under unbounded at-least-once retry. A safe-but-not-idempotent writer preserves log integrity invariants but allows duplicate entries to accumulate. Over time, with network partitions causing repeated retries, the log grows without bound relative to the number of distinct events. This resource exhaustion violates a liveness/operational property even though safety invariants hold. Therefore, the writer must be idempotent \u2014 it must detect that an event was already appended and refuse the duplicate \u2014 to guarantee both correctness and bounded resource use. The causal mechanism: retry \u2192 idempotent check (event ID already in log?) \u2192 skip duplicate \u2192 log remains proportional to distinct events.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
